summary: This release upgrades OSpec from a document-driven change workflow into a one-change native-agent execution platform with task graphs, native harness launch plans, task-level reviews, evidence gates, and hardened release safety.
new: Added first-class one-change task graph execution with dispatch, launch planning, completion collection, retry, blocker escalation, and controller status commands.
Added native harness launch metadata for Codex/GPT, Claude Code, Gemini, and OpenCode so current-harness subagents are the default worker path.
Added task-level spec and quality review gates before dependent work can dispatch, plus final whole-change review gates.
Added durable TDD, debugging, and verification evidence artifacts that can be archive-gated by workflow flags.
Added project session, bootstrap, handoff, workspace, worktree, finish, brainstorm, and plan helper commands for safer AI-assisted change execution.
improved: Kept one active change as the normal entry point while supporting parallel-safe worker batches and stronger controller guidance.
Improved execute status and next output so the next worker, review, verification, or blocker action is visible without reading raw artifacts.
Improved generated AI guidance, packaged skills, project conventions, and public usage docs for the new one-change agent workflow.
fixed: Fixed release smoke coverage so generated smoke changes satisfy task graph, review, worker status, and verification evidence archive gates.
Clarified that CLI worker command execution is fallback-only when native harness subagents are unavailable or explicitly bypassed.
docs: Documented the one-change native-agent execution flow in the README and usage guides.
Added release metadata for GitHub Release notes and local release-note preview.
